additions.name: Content Credentials Verify
additions.description: Upload an image, video, or PDF to read its C2PA manifest chain: signer identity, generative-AI training/edit assertions, and thumbnail history.
additions.notes: A valid signature only proves the manifest chain was unmodified after signing, not that the depicted scene is real; C2PA's Interim Trust List (ITL) was frozen as of January 2026 pending the full Trust List rollout, so some legitimately-signed media may show as untrusted.

additions.name: SynthID Detector
additions.description: Checks whether an image, audio clip, video, or text was generated or edited with Google AI tools by scanning for the invisible SynthID watermark.
additions.notes: Only detects SynthID-watermarked content from Google's own models (Gemini, Imagen, Veo, Lyria), not other generators; Google claims >99% detection on raw outputs but independent tests show recovery drops to roughly 68-95% after heavy compression, cropping, or downscaling below ~512px.

additions.name: Forensically
additions.description: Free browser-based suite of image forensic filters (error level analysis, clone detection, noise analysis, metadata, and now C2PA manifest reading).
additions.notes: Creator explicitly warns to treat any C2PA signature it displays 'with a big pinch of salt' since remote-manifest fetching is disabled for security reasons; ELA and clone-detection outputs are hypothesis-generating only and must be corroborated with other methods.

additions.name: FotoForensics
additions.description: Upload a JPEG or PNG to run Error Level Analysis and metadata checks that flag regions with inconsistent compression history.
additions.notes: Still active and unchanged since 2025 snapshot. ELA only detects JPEG re-save inconsistencies, not lossless-format edits or manipulations that equalize compression; screenshots, HDR, and smartphone processing all mimic manipulation signals, and uploading evidentiary images to this third-party server breaks chain of custody for casework.

additions.name: Fake News Debunker (InVID-WeVerify, vera.ai)
additions.description: Browser extension for keyframe extraction, reverse image/video search, magnifier/forensic filters, and beta synthetic-media and voice-clone detectors.
additions.notes: Actively maintained under EU Horizon project vera.ai (successor to WeVerify/InVID), not discontinued; Chrome build reached v0.92 (June 2026) and Firefox v0.89.1 (March 2026), adding a WACZ-based archiving module and a beta audio voice-clone detector built on Hiya/Loccus tech. Synthetic-media detector modules remain beta-quality; treat scores as investigative leads, not verdicts.

additions.name: NVIDIA Synthetic Video Detector
additions.description: NIM microservice that scores video frames for AI-generation likelihood using DINOv2/DINOv3 vision-transformer backbones, deployed via partner platforms.
additions.notes: Not directly available to the public; accessed only through partner integrations such as Wowza Video Intelligence and Dalet Flex. NVIDIA reports 92% accuracy on uncompressed video falling to 87% at 15% compression and 82% at 50% compression (internal AUC 0.96); explicitly positioned by NVIDIA as a frame-level triage signal, not a courtroom-grade verdict.

additions.name: Hiya Deepfake Voice Detector
additions.description: Real-time and file-based audio analysis that flags AI voice cloning and synthetic speech, integrated into newsroom verification workflows via vera.ai.
additions.notes: Built on technology from Loccus (Spanish voice-security startup acquired by Hiya); primarily sold as an enterprise anti-fraud API rather than a free public checker, and independent third-party accuracy benchmarks for newsroom use cases are not publicly published.

additions.name: TinEye
additions.description: Reverse image search engine specialized in finding the earliest known occurrence of a picture across its indexed web crawl.
additions.notes: Strong for exact/near-duplicate matches and first-seen dating, but weak at facial matching (independent comparisons put face-match accuracy around 25-40%) and its index is far smaller than Google's or Yandex's.

additions.name: Yandex Images
additions.description: Reverse image search engine indexing a large share of Russian-language and Eastern European web and social content, with facial similarity matching.
additions.notes: Repeatedly cited by OSINT practitioners as the best free option for Russian/CIS-region sources and casual facial matching, but independent tests put its facial-match accuracy around only 65-75%, well below dedicated facial-recognition tools.

additions.name: PimEyes
additions.description: Dedicated facial-recognition search engine that finds other web images containing an uploaded face.
additions.notes: Vendor claims 99.5% accuracy; independent comparisons put real-world facial accuracy closer to 85-95%. Under continuing regulatory scrutiny from the EDPB, UK ICO, French CNIL, and German DPAs over non-consensual facial recognition; verify current-jurisdiction legality before use.

additions.name: Google Lens
additions.description: Visual search that finds matching or visually similar images across the web, now the primary interface for reverse image lookups on mobile.
additions.notes: Google has consolidated reverse image search into Lens; the standalone 'search by image' button in mobile browser results has been phased out, so investigators on mobile now need the Lens app or camera icon rather than the classic desktop-style reverse search flow.

additions.name: Google Fact Check Explorer
additions.description: Search engine over the global ClaimReview-tagged fact-check corpus, filterable by publisher, language, and date.
additions.notes: Coverage depends entirely on publishers correctly marking up ClaimReview schema; smaller regional fact-checkers without technical SEO support may be underrepresented.

additions.name: Google Fact Check Tools API
additions.description: REST API (claims:search, claims:imageSearch) to programmatically query the same ClaimReview corpus that powers Fact Check Explorer.
additions.notes: Free with a Google API key and modest quota; the imageSearch endpoint lets you query fact checks by uploading an image rather than text.

additions.name: Ad Fontes Interactive Media Bias Chart
additions.description: Searchable chart rating roughly 4,800 news websites, podcasts, and TV shows for political bias and factual reliability using multi-analyst human review.
additions.notes: Free interactive chart exposes only the ~250 top-rated sources with a daily search cap; searching the full 4,800-source dataset or accessing daily AI-assisted ratings requires a paid News Nerd/data-platform subscription.

additions.name: IFCN Signatories Directory
additions.description: Directory of fact-checking organizations that have been vetted and certified against the International Fact-Checking Network's Code of Principles.
additions.notes: Useful for vetting whether a regional fact-checker is independently verified; certification does not guarantee every individual fact check is error-free, only that the organization's process was audited.

additions.name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
additions.description: Free public web archive that captures, timestamps, and replays historical snapshots of URLs, with a 'Save Page Now' capture-on-demand feature.
additions.notes: Unchanged core service, but heavy JavaScript-rendered pages and paywalled or social-platform content often capture incompletely; not itself cryptographically signed, so pair with a hashing tool for evidentiary use.

additions.name: archive.today
additions.description: On-demand webpage snapshot tool that produces a permanent, timestamped mirror URL, commonly used to preserve pages likely to be edited or deleted.
additions.notes: No official API and rotates domains (archive.ph/archive.today/archive.is); capture success is rate-limited and can be blocked by sites that detect the archiver's user agent.

additions.name: Perma.cc / Scoop Capture Engine
additions.description: Harvard Library Innovation Lab's browser-based capture engine that produces signed WARC/WACZ archives with full provenance metadata for legal citation.
additions.notes: Scoop supports cryptographic WACZ signing/verification for chain-of-custody, built for legal citation use cases; Perma.cc itself (the hosted permalink service) is free for most academic/legal users but has usage limits for non-affiliated accounts.

additions.name: Hunchly
additions.description: Desktop investigation tool that automatically captures, hashes (SHA-256), and GPG-signs every webpage visited, then assembles court-ready evidence packages.
additions.notes: Vendor's own evidence guide discloses that its GPG signing can theoretically be defeated by someone with local access to the private key store, and recommends independent corroboration (e.g., checking Wayback Machine) rather than relying on hashes/signatures alone.

additions.name: Trawlr
additions.description: Self-hosted open-source platform for archiving Telegram channels/groups, tracking edits and deletions, extracting entities, and alerting on watchlist matches.
additions.notes: Requires self-hosting and a Telegram account/API credentials; SHA-256 deduplication and entity-extraction watchlists make it suited to ongoing monitoring rather than one-off captures.

additions.name: tg-archiver
additions.description: Self-hosted Telegram channel archiver with full-text search, translation, RSS feeds, and forward-chain tracking to auto-discover related channels.
additions.notes: Built by OSINT Ukraine researchers for conflict-monitoring use cases; requires Docker/PostgreSQL/Redis self-hosting, no hosted SaaS version.

additions.name: Etherscan API v2 (Multichain)
additions.description: Unified block-explorer API providing balances, transactions, and contract data across 50+ EVM chains from a single API key.
additions.notes: Free tier now capped at 3 calls/sec, 100,000 calls/day, and only 'selected chains (90% coverage)' via community endpoints only; full multichain coverage and API Pro endpoints (needed for richer address-tagging data) require paid tiers starting at $49/month, a narrowing from the prior single-chain free access model.

additions.name: Arkham Intelligence
additions.description: Free-to-browse blockchain intelligence platform that links wallet addresses to real-world entities and visualizes fund flows across chains.
additions.notes: Entity attributions are crowdsourced/algorithmic and not always independently verified; treat labels as investigative leads, especially for newly tagged addresses.

additions.name: Blockchair
additions.description: Multi-chain block explorer and search engine covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, and 15+ other networks with cross-chain address and transaction search.
additions.notes: Free web search is unlimited for casual lookups but bulk data exports and the API require a paid plan.

additions.name: OFAC Sanctions List Search
additions.description: US Treasury tool to search the SDN and other sanctions lists by name, entity, or identifier, including listed cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
additions.notes: Only covers US sanctions designations; a clean result does not mean an address is unsanctioned under other jurisdictions' lists (EU, UK OFSI, UN).

changes.name: InVID/WeVerify Verification Plugin
changes.detail: Rebranded and continued under the EU vera.ai project as 'Fake News Debunker'; the tool is actively maintained (Chrome v0.92, June 2026; Firefox v0.89.1, March 2026) and not discontinued as sometimes assumed.

changes.name: Google Reverse Image Search (mobile)
changes.detail: The standalone 'search by image' entry point on mobile browsers has been folded into the Google Lens app/camera icon, removing the classic desktop-style reverse-image workflow from mobile Search.

changes.name: Etherscan Free API Tier
changes.detail: With the migration to unified Etherscan API v2, the free tier is now limited to community endpoints and roughly 90% chain coverage; full multichain access and API Pro data (address metadata, higher rate limits) require paid plans from $49/month.

changes.name: Chainalysis Free Tools
changes.detail: Chainalysis no longer offers a public free tier; Reactor, KYT, and Kryptos are sold exclusively as quote-based enterprise subscriptions priced by seats, blockchain coverage, and transaction volume.
